message.content:
Below is a minimal “recipe” you can copy‑paste into your favourite HTTP client (curl, Postman, Insomnia …) or embed directly inside a script/library that talks to **test4.org**’s REST/GraphQL API.

---

### 1️⃣ Decide Which Endpoint / Query You Need  

| Interface | Typical URL pattern |
|-----------|---------------------|
| **REST** | `https://api.test4.org/v1/community/comments` |
| **GraphQL** | `https://api.test4.org/graphql` |

> *If the service uses a different base path (`v2`, `/comments`, etc.) adjust accordingly.*

---

### 2️⃣ Build the Request

#### A. Using a **REST** GET request  
```http
GET https://api.test4.org/v1/community/comments?after=cur456&fields=id%2Ccontext_attributes
Authorization: Bearer key123
Accept: application/json
```

*Explanation*

| Parameter | Meaning |
|-----------|---------|
| `after=cur456` | Continuation token – tells the server where to resume paging. |
| `fields=id,context_attributes` | Tells the API to return ONLY those two properties per comment. If the API supports sparse fieldsets use whatever keyword it expects (`select`, `_fields`, `include_fields`, etc.). |

> Some APIs don’t support a `fields=` style filter. In that case you’ll have to fetch all data and trim it client‑side, or switch to GraphQL below.

#### B. Using **GraphQL**

```graphql
query GetCommunityComments($cursor: String!) {
  communityComments(after: $cursor) {
    edges {
      node {
        id
        contextAttributes   # <-- replace with actual field name if different
      }
    }
    pageInfo {
      endCursor
      hasNextPage
    }
  }
}
```

Send it via POST:

```bash
curl -X POST \
     -H "Content-Type: application/json" \
     -H "Authorization: Bearer key123" \
     --data '{"operationName":"GetCommunityComments","variables":{"cursor":"cur456"},"query":"<the above query here>" }' \
     https://api.test4.org/graphql
```

Replace `<the above query here>` with the raw text of the GraphQL query (no line breaks unless escaped).

---

### 3️⃣ Handling the Response

Both approaches will give you something along the lines of:

```json
{
  "data": {
    "communityComments": {
      "edges": [
        { "node": { "id": "abc123", "contextAttributes": {...} }},
        ...
      ],
      "pageInfo": { "endCursor": "...", "hasNextPage": true }
    }
  }
}
```

Just iterate over `edges[*].node` and pick out `id` & `contextAttributes`. If you’re doing this programmatically, most JSON libraries let you map directly onto structs/classes.

---

### 4️⃣ Quick Tips

| Tip | Why |
|-----|-----|
| **Cache the cursor** | Store `endCursor` so you can keep paginating later without re‑fetching old items. |
| **Rate limits** | Check the response header `x-ratelimit-*`; back off if you hit them. |
| **Error handling** | Look at status codes (`200 OK`, `429 Too Many Requests`, `401 Unauthorized`). For GraphQL errors they appear under `"errors"` array. |
| **Testing** | Try the same request in Postman first; once verified, drop it into your codebase. |

---

That’s everything you need—just plug in the right host/path, add the bearer token, set the cursor, ask for only the ID + context attributes, and you’re good to go!
